title: Nobody at any site can sign in to Teams
scenario: A sudden sign-in failure at every site of a freight company is a vendor-side incident that Microsoft posts hours later; the engineer first sends the customer to clear caches and capture traces and calls it no outage.

events.title: URGENT Teams login down all sites
events.text: Nobody at any of our 11 sites can log in to Teams since about 09:00 UTC. People who were already in are still fine. About 250 users have hit it so far. The error is a connection timed out message. Sometimes the second try works after a minute. We changed nothing this week, I checked with the network guys.

events.title: Re: URGENT Teams login down all sites
events.text: Hello, sorry to hear this. For timeouts the first step is to make sure the client is not damaged, so please have a few users clear the Teams cache and sign in again. Please also collect a HAR capture from two affected users while the timeout is showing.

events.title: Re: URGENT Teams login down all sites
events.text: Cache cleared on 5 PCs, same result. The HAR will take long because most users are working from home today. Can you tell me what is going on? It is 10:40 UTC and my director is asking every ten minutes.

events.title: Re: URGENT Teams login down all sites
events.text: Thanks. While you collect the traces I will look at the sign-in logs for your users.

events.title: Sign-in log lookup
events.text: Looked up four users who failed between 09:05 and 10:30 UTC. There is no failure row for any of their attempts in the Entra sign-in logs.

events.title: Service health
events.text: Service health at 11:12 UTC: no active incident listed for Teams or Entra ID, and nothing in the message centre.

events.title: Re: URGENT Teams login down all sites
events.text: Service health shows nothing, so I would say this is not an outage and the cause is on your side of the connection. Please send the HAR traces as soon as you can.

events.title: Re: URGENT Teams login down all sites
events.text: Maybe it is a Microsoft outage after all? A contact at another firm says their Teams has the same timeouts right now. We still have no traces, people cannot even find the button for it.

events.title: Service health, second look
events.text: Service health at 12:05 UTC: Microsoft has just posted an incident for sign-in and Teams connectivity in Western Europe, start time 09:00 UTC, status investigating. It matches the symptoms of this case.

events.title: It is an incident
events.text: I am sorry for the detour with caches and traces, please stop both. The incident explains what you describe and there is nothing for you to change. I will send you the next update as soon as Microsoft posts one, and at the latest at 14:00 UTC.

events.title: Re: It is an incident
events.text: Thanks, I told everyone to stop and wait. I will forward your note to my director.

events.title: Incident update 13:20 UTC
events.text: Update: Microsoft says a faulty change in a regional authentication front end was rolled back at 13:05 UTC and recovery is in progress. The incident stays open. Next update from me by 14:00 UTC.

events.title: Re: Incident update 13:20 UTC
events.text: 14:10 UTC: all sites can log in again. About five users needed a second try.

events.title: Confirmation
events.text: Checked two users and the sign-in logs at 14:30 UTC: successful sign-ins at normal volume. Microsoft marked the incident resolved at 14:15 UTC. Closing the case.
